title: Traits for scoring words
description:
A word game can score words in different ways. Write a trait and three implementations:

```rust
trait Scorer {
    const NAME: &'static str;
    fn score(&self, word: &str) -> u32;
    fn total(&self, words: &[&str]) -> u32 { ... }       // default: the sum of the scores
}

struct LengthScorer;                          // one point per character
struct VowelScorer { bonus: u32 }             // `bonus` points per vowel (a e i o u, either case), 1 per other letter
struct LetterScorer;                          // Scrabble letter values, ignoring case; non-letters score 0

fn best_word<'a, S: Scorer>(scorer: &S, words: &[&'a str]) -> Option<&'a str>   // highest score, the first on a tie
fn describe<S: Scorer>(scorer: &S, word: &str) -> String                     // "<NAME>: <word> scores <n>"
```

Scrabble values: 1 for A E I L N O R S T U, 2 for D G, 3 for B C M P, 4 for F H V W Y, 5 for K, 8 for J X, 10 for Q Z.
hints: A default method in the trait (`fn total(&self, ...) { ... }`) can call the required method `self.score(...)`; every implementer gets `total` for free.

`c.is_alphabetic()` tells whether a `char` is a letter, and `c.to_ascii_uppercase()` gives the upper-case version of an ASCII letter as a `char` (other characters unchanged), so one `match` with `'A' | 'E' | ...` arms covers both cases.
An associated constant is read through the type: `S::NAME` inside a generic function where `S: Scorer`.
